subject: Shouldn't log likelihood always be normalized by data size in bayesian estimation?

messages.author: 39971e2c19b8ec70
messages.subject: Shouldn't log likelihood always be normalized by data size in bayesian estimation?
parts:
Hello everyone,

This is a deeper statistical question which I am wrapping my head
around for some time, and would be very grateful for help. I wonder
if the whole bayesian statistics is neglecting it or if I am super
confused.

In bayesian statistics, we are looking at this distribution p(y|theta)
* p(theta). In the point estimation like MAP, we are looking at:

log p(y|theta) + log p(theta)

but, while the magnitude of the prior will not change with data size;
while the magnitude of log likelihood will! Which, if we think about
the prior as about something, which penalizes the complexity of the
model, will change the weight of this penalization based just on data
size.

Please follow the details of the questions in here:
https://stats.stackexchange.com/q/462076/5509

I would be very grateful for some directions!

Thanks and have a great day!

Tomas
